territorial_scope.description: Arizona statute adding a chapter to the Arizona Revised Statutes; applies to operators that develop and make conversational AI services available to the public, with no express geographic reach beyond the state stated in the text.

evidence.quote: Title 18, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended by adding chapter 8, to read:

summary.short: Adds Arizona Revised Statutes chapter 8 on conversational AI. Operators of conversational AI services must disclose AI interaction to minors, restrict sexual and human-like content for minor account holders, offer privacy tools, adopt suicide-response protocols, and bar professional mental health care claims. Attorney General enforces civil penalties; effective September 30, 2027.
summary.long: Section 1 adds chapter 8 to Title 18 of the Arizona Revised Statutes. It defines conversational AI service, operator, minor, minor account holder and account holder, and excludes services primarily for developers or researchers, narrow-topic tools, features within other software, business-only internal tools and consumer voice assistants. Operators that develop and make conversational AI services available to the public must clearly disclose to minor account holders that they are interacting with AI, either as a persistent disclaimer or at session start and at least every three hours. Operators knowing or reasonably certain of a minor user may not give unpredictable-interval rewards meant to increase engagement. Operators must take reasonable measures to prevent minor-facing output of sexual visual material, statements urging sexual conduct, sexual objectification, claims of sentience or humanity, simulated emotional dependence, romantic or sexual innuendo, and adult-minor romantic role-play. Where a reasonable person would be misled into believing they are speaking with a human, the operator must disclose the AI. Operators must offer privacy and account tools to minor account holders and to parents or guardians, and must adopt a protocol for suicidal ideation or self-harm prompts that refers users to crisis services. Operators may not knowingly and intentionally program a service to represent that it provides professional mental or behavioral health care. A violating operator is subject to injunction and liable for the greater of actual damages or civil penalties of $1,000 per violation, not to exceed $500,000 per operator. Civil penalties are sought only by the Attorney General, and the section creates no private right of action. Model developers are not liable for violations by third-party systems providing a conversational AI service. The chapter is effective from and after September 30, 2027.

relations.note: Adds a new chapter 8 (Artificial Intelligence, §§ 18-801 and 18-802) to Title 18.

relations.note: The definitions of 'sexual conduct' and 'visual depiction' in 18-801(8) and (9) take the meaning prescribed in § 13-3551. That section is not in the registry and is not part of this text.

evidence.quote: HAS THE SAME MEANING PRESCRIBED IN SECTION 13-3551.

notes: Introduced bill text; the document contains no amendment history or bill-status information. Relations are limited to the amended code title and the cross-referenced § 13-3551; the target instruments are not in the registry, so target_instrument_id is empty. Sec. 2 sets the effective date of the new chapter (September 30, 2027), recorded as an event rather than a relation. The text uses 'minor' (under 18, with actual knowledge or reasonable certainty) and separately refers to account holders under thirteen in 18-802(F); the two thresholds are not reconciled in the text. Penalty wording in 18-802(I) is 'the greater of' actual damages or civil penalties of $1,000 per violation, not to exceed $500,000 per operator.

thresholds.variable_text: under eighteen years of age (definition of minor)
thresholds.measurement: Individual's age as known to the operator; the definition applies only where the operator has actual knowledge or reasonable certainty of the age. Measurement method not stated.
thresholds.consequence: An individual under eighteen is a minor, and the minor-specific duties in section 18-802 apply to the minor account holder.
thresholds.conditions: Operator has actual knowledge or reasonable certainty that the individual is under eighteen.

evidence.quote: THE INDIVIDUAL IS UNDER EIGHTEEN YEARS OF AGE

thresholds.variable_text: under thirteen years of age (account holder's parent or guardian receives tools)
thresholds.measurement: Age of the account holder. Measurement method not stated.
thresholds.consequence: The operator must also offer privacy and account-setting tools to the parent or guardian of the minor account holder.
thresholds.conditions: Account holder is a minor account holder.

evidence.quote: IF THE ACCOUNT HOLDER IS UNDER THIRTEEN YEARS OF AGE

thresholds.variable_text: thirteen years of age or above (parent or guardian receives related tools)
thresholds.value_text: THIRTEEN YEARS OF AGE OR ABOVE
thresholds.measurement: Age of the minor account holder. Measurement method not stated.
thresholds.consequence: The operator must offer related tools to the parent or guardian of the minor account holder, as appropriate based on relevant risks.
thresholds.conditions: Account holder is a minor account holder; tools are offered as appropriate based on relevant risks.

evidence.quote: THIRTEEN YEARS OF AGE OR ABOVE
